key_insight: ProjectionBench measures how well LLMs generate scientific hypotheses as progressively more experimental information is revealed, separating novelty under sparse context from grounded reasoning under full context.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark offers a practical way to compare and improve AI scientist systems for materials and other discovery workflows, especially when models must reason from incomplete problem statements.
method: Start with only a paper’s topic and research question.
Reveal details stepwise up to the classical null-hypothesis test.
Score model hypotheses against paper conclusions using semantic similarity over atomic claims.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated GPT-5, GPT-5.4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview on 45 papers across bioactive materials, mechanical materials, and nanomaterials, and report GPT-5.4 reached about 0.7 F1 alignment with ground-truth conclusions even under minimal context.
watch_item: Semantic-similarity scoring may miss scientifically valid but differently framed hypotheses, so the benchmark should be used with care when comparing models that express conclusions in diverse ways.
paper_title: ProjectionBench: Evaluating Scientific Hypothesis Generation in LLMs Under Progressive Information Disclosure
